question: On neurological examination of a patient with chronic daily headache, which ONE finding on fundoscopy would MOST strongly indicate raised intracranial pressure requiring urgent investigation?

answers.text: Small, round optic disc with clear margins

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A small, well-defined optic disc with clear margins is normal and does not indicate raised intracranial pressure.

answers.text: Blurring of the optic disc margins with loss of venous pulsation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Papilloedema — characterised by blurring of optic disc margins, elevation of the disc, obliteration of the central cup, and loss of spontaneous venous pulsations — is the fundoscopic hallmark of raised intracranial pressure.

Incorrect. AV nipping indicates hypertensive retinopathy, not raised intracranial pressure specifically. While hypertension can cause headache, AV nipping alone is not the specific sign of raised ICP.
Incorrect. Optic atrophy with a pale disc and sharp margins suggests previous optic nerve damage but is not the sign of acute raised intracranial pressure.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key fundoscopic sign of raised ICP is papilloedema: blurring of optic disc margins and loss of spontaneous venous pulsation. Always perform fundoscopy in a headache patient before LP.
Well done. Papilloedema (blurred disc margins + loss of venous pulsation) is the fundoscopic sign of raised ICP. It mandates urgent neuroimaging before lumbar puncture.
